recognize_zh: 紅血球大小正常，內含多個紫紅色裂殖子（merozoites）圍繞一團棕黑色瘧色素（hemozoin）的裂殖體（schizont），旁邊紅血球可見細小環狀體；嗜中性球與單核球胞質內也吞有棕黑色色素顆粒，符合重度惡性瘧（P. falciparum）感染。
features: Mature schizonts within normal-sized, non-stippled red cells containing numerous small magenta merozoites clustered around a single dark brown-black pigment mass
Ruptured/rupturing schizont with free merozoites scattered adjacent to a pigment clump
Delicate ring form with a small chromatin dot in a neighboring red cell
Hemozoin (malaria pigment) phagocytosed within a neutrophil and within a monocyte
Host red cells not enlarged and lacking Schüffner stippling
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows red cells infected by mature schizonts containing multiple merozoites arranged around a single clump of dark brown-black pigment; one schizont appears ruptured with free merozoites. A delicate ring form is present in an adjacent erythrocyte, and infected red cells are of normal size without Schüffner dots. Brown-black hemozoin pigment is also seen within the cytoplasm of a neutrophil and a monocyte. Findings are consistent with Plasmodium falciparum infection; circulating schizonts and pigment-laden leukocytes indicate high parasite burden and severe malaria.

ddx.vs: P. vivax schizonts carry 12–24 larger merozoites in an enlarged red cell with Schüffner stippling, whereas falciparum-infected cells are normal-sized and schizonts are rarely seen in blood except in severe infection.
P. malariae forms rosette schizonts with about 8 merozoites around central pigment in small-to-normal red cells and shows band forms, with fewer ring forms.
Morphology overlaps (rings like falciparum, mature stages like malariae), so PCR and travel history to Southeast Asia are needed to separate it.
Babesia rings lack hemozoin pigment and schizonts and may form tetrad (Maltese cross) arrangements.
